title: Pacerchain e2e latency census and cohort field notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for the

Pacerchain e2e latency census. This is a hands-on trace synthesis + sampling pass intended to surface which stages contribute to tail behavior across realistic cohorts. Not a polished report — this is the operational notebook I used while investigating the odd p99s observed during the October rollout spike.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Two dominant tail phenotypes: (A) batching/emit backpressure causing long residence in the emit handoff (often visible as long gaps between last GPU token and first egress byte); (B) KV-cache cold-paths + routing fallback causing an extra 200–800ms in ~0.4% of traces.
- Short seq cohort (<=64 tokens): median ~48ms, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~480ms. Emit-stage and network egress explain ~65% of p99 headroom.
- Long seq cohort (>512 tokens): median ~260ms, p95 ~900ms, p99 ~2.6s. GPU inference dominates median and p95; p99 is a mixture of GPU queue jitter and downstream batching handoffs.

Experiment setup and dataset:
- Time window: 2024-10-01 to 2024-10-10 (production sampled traces), plus targeted replay of 25k synthetic traces on staging cluster v5.2-rc.
- Sampling: SLO sampler configured at 2% for p95-triggered captures, plus additional smell-based sampler for KV miss events.
- Workloads: mix of chat-like (prompt+history avg 48 tokens) and single-turn generation (prompt avg 28 tokens), plus long-document summarization flows (avg 900 tokens emitted).
- Hardware: A100 farms (multi-GPU nodes), some older V100 pools in fallback region eu-west-1b. Kernel builds: optimized kernel set A for A100, generic kernel set B used for V100.

Cohort definitions used in census:
- short-seq: request.output_len_est <= 64
- mid-seq: 64 < request.output_len_est <= 512
- long-seq: request.output_len_est > 512
- kv-hit / kv-miss split (per-request)

Representative per-stage breakdowns (aggregated numbers, median/p95/p99 in ms). These are synthesized from sampled traces and replayed runs; they match production telemetry within +/-10% on medians but can differ for tails.

SHORT-SEQ COHORT (<=64 tokens) - sample N=18,372
- Total e2e: p50 48ms | p95 130ms | p99 480ms
  - client-ingest (parse+auth): p50 6 | p95 12 | p99 30
  - route/routing-decision: p50 2 | p95 5 | p99 20
  - queue-to-batcher (wait): p50 4 | p95 18 | p99 160
  - tokenize + encode: p50 3 | p95 9 | p99 25
  - kv-lookup (hit): p50 2 | p95 6 | p99 40
  - gpu-infer (first-token latency + kv-apply): p50 18 | p95 50 | p99 140
  - emit-handoff (handoff to egress writers / streaming): p50 6 | p95 18 | p99 240
  - egress (network + SSL + client ack): p50 7 | p95 12 | p99 85

Notes: p99 blowups mostly live in queue-to-batcher and emit-handoff. Traces with queue waits >150ms often correlate with microburst arrivals (many small requests created by clients sending turns in rapid succession). Emit-handoff p99s show repeated 50–200ms spikes when the egress writer pool gets saturated and retries/backpressure kick in.

LONG-SEQ COHORT (>512 tokens) - sample N=3,104
- Total e2e: p50 260ms | p95 900ms | p99 2600ms
  - client-ingest: p50 10 | p95 22 | p99 60
  - route-decision: p50 3 | p95 8 | p99 35
  - queue-to-batcher: p50 10 | p95 60 | p99 420
  - tokenizer + encode: p50 6 | p95 18 | p99 60
  - kv-lookup (misses much more common in this cohort): p50 12 | p95 80 | p99 420
  - gpu-infer (bulk tokens; includes KV-apply overhead): p50 180 | p95 600 | p99 1800
  - streaming/emit: p50 25 | p95 80 | p99 360
  - egress: p50 14 | p95 30 | p99 245

Notes: Long-seq p99 dominated by two sub-phenotypes: (1) KV miss cascades (locking while filling large prefixes into KV store), and (2) GPU scheduling jitter—large models occupy slots longer, and when a GPU node experiences transient GC or kernel preemption, queue depths spike and waiting requests accumulate.

Trace-level observations (selected examples):
- Trace A (short-seq, p99): queue-to-batcher 320ms + emit-handoff 190ms. Client produced burst of 11 concurrent small requests — batcher took several scheduling cycles to pack them, leaving one request behind repeatedly. Suggestion: consider latency-first packing in bursty mode (short-window, low batch cap) when we detect high fan-in from a single client IP.
- Trace B (long-seq, p99): KV miss during early prefix creation triggered synchronous store-write of ~380ms; GPU inference then queued and added 900ms due to slot contention. The store-write was to the remote memcached cluster in a different AZ; we saw a cross-AZ tail at the same timestamp. Suggestion: re-evaluate our KV replication affinity; prefer local-az writes for hot-prefixes or convert to async write-with-retry for non-critical KV metadata.
- Trace C (mid-seq, p95 spike): emit-handoff repeated backoff loop when egress writer returned EAGAIN due to ephemeral file descriptors exhaustion (tracked to a socket leak in emitter pool). Fix already in PR 4521 but leaving note here.

Hypotheses tested in staging replays:
1) Reducing batcher max-wait from 20ms -> 5ms reduces short-seq p99 by ~40% at cost of ~6% throughput; improves latency for single-client bursts.
2) KV local-az preference decreases KV miss tail by ~60% for long-seq scenarios tied to memcached coldsets.
3) Increasing emitter writer pool from 12 -> 24 threads reduces emit-handoff p99 by ~35% for short-seq; CPU saturation observed if we scale beyond 32 without increasing egress worker nodes.

Actionable next steps (short list):
- Deploy batcher adaptive policy: when fan-in from same client > 8 requests/s, switch to latency-first window (5ms) for that client token. (Owner: Diego)
- Add an async write path + best-effort local cache for KV stores used during prefix construction to reduce synchronous remote writes. (Owner: Mikhail)
- Monitor emitter fd/socket usage; roll out PR 4521 to production canary and keep the emitter pool at +25% capacity in eu-west-1b for 72 hours. (Owner: Kristin)
- Add a p99 per-stage alert that can drive an automated temporary capacity burst: if emit-handoff p99 > 400ms for 10m, auto-scale additional egress writers (safety cap 3x).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why do a small fraction (~0.05%) of short-seq traces show queue-to-batcher > 1s even when overall QPS is modest? Need deeper trace correlation with host-level events (OOM killers, node reboots, network partitions).
- Explore kernel-set differences: do V100 nodes emit systematically wider tails? We have hints that generic kernel set B produces more stalls for certain attention patterns. Run targeted microbenchmarks for kernel A vs B for tail behavior.

Appendix (short):
- Replay run IDs: replay-20241007-01 (25k synth) ; replay-20241009-03 (kv-miss-heavy)
- Quick links: JIRA-3872 (batcher-modes), PR-4521 (emitter-fd-fix), confluence/pacerchain-design.

Notes to self: this doc is a snapshot—I'll convert the mitigations into a short RFC after the PRs land. Keep sampling window at 3% for another week post-rollout.
